verses.text: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham, who was coming back after defeating the kings, and he blessed him.
Abraham gave him a tenth of everything he had won. First, the name Melchizedek means "king of what is right". Also, king of Salem means "king of peace".
Nothing is written about his father, his mother or his family. There is no record of when he was born or when he died. Like the Son of God, he stays a priest forever.
Think how great this man was! Even Abraham, the father of our nation, gave him a tenth of the best things he had won in battle.
The law says the priests from the family of Levi must collect a tenth from the people, that is, from their own relatives, even though they all come from Abraham.
But Melchizedek did not come from Levi's family, yet he collected a tenth from Abraham. And he blessed Abraham, the one who had God's promises.
Everyone agrees that the person who blesses is greater than the one who is blessed.
The priests who collect a tenth are people who die. But Scripture says that Melchizedek lives on.
We could even say that Levi, whose family collects the tenth, paid a tenth through Abraham.
Levi was not born yet. He was still in the body of his ancestor Abraham when Melchizedek met him.

The people were given the law under the priests from Levi's family. If those priests could have made people perfect, why was another priest needed, one in the line of Melchizedek and not in the line of Aaron?
When the priesthood changes, the law must change too.
The one we are talking about belongs to a different tribe. No one from that tribe has ever served as a priest at the altar.
It is clear that our Lord came from the tribe of Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests from that tribe.
This becomes even clearer when another priest appears who is like Melchizedek.
He became a priest, not because of a law about his family line, but because of the power of a life that cannot be destroyed.
For Scripture says, "You are a priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek."
So the old rule has been set aside, because it was weak and useless.
The law never made anything perfect. But now a better hope has been given, and through it we come close to God.
And God made Jesus a priest with an oath.

Other priests became priests without an oath, but Jesus became a priest with an oath, when God said to him, "The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: 'You are a priest forever, in the line of Melchizedek.'"
Because of this oath, Jesus is our guarantee of a better covenant.
There were many of those other priests, because death stopped each of them from continuing.
But Jesus lives forever, so his priesthood never ends.
That is why he can save completely those who come to God through him. He lives forever to speak to God for them.
Jesus is the High Priest we need. He is holy, without blame and pure. He is set apart from sinners and raised higher than the heavens.

He does not need to offer sacrifices every day like the other high priests, first for their own sins and then for the sins of the people. He offered a sacrifice once for all time, when he offered himself.
The law chooses high priests who are weak men. But God's oath, which came after the law, chose the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
